base_cards.front: How many compulsory bullets are in the 90-word task?
back: Three.

base_cards.front: How many compulsory bullets are in the 150-word task?
back: Two.

base_cards.front: Translate: parce que.
back: Because.

base_cards.front: Translate: cependant.
back: However.

base_cards.front: Complete: J'aime ___ (lire / lis).
back: lire.

base_cards.front: Complete: Je vais ___ (jouer / joué).
back: jouer.

base_cards.front: Complete: J'ai ___ (jouer / joué).
back: joué.

base_cards.front: Translate: à mon avis.
back: In my opinion.

base_cards.front: Complete: beaucoup ___ livres.
back: de.

base_cards.front: Translate: pour protéger.
back: To protect / in order to protect.

base_cards.front: Write I would like to help in French.
back: Je voudrais aider.

base_cards.front: Write I prefer reading because it is relaxing in French.
back: Je préfère lire parce que c'est relaxant.

base_cards.front: Write Yesterday, I visited a town in French.
back: Hier, j'ai visité une ville.

base_cards.front: Write Tomorrow, I am going to work in French.
back: Demain, je vais travailler.

base_cards.front: Correct: Mes amis est gentil.
back: Mes amis **sont gentils**.
The subject, verb and adjective must agree.

base_cards.front: Correct: Elle est allé en France.
back: Elle est **allée** en France.
The past participle agrees with the feminine subject after être.

base_cards.front: Translate into French: I have no brothers.
back: Je n'ai pas de frères.
Use de after this negative.

base_cards.front: What should a writing plan record for each compulsory bullet?
back: A direct answer and relevant development, such as a reason, example or detail. Identify any requested time frame too.

base_cards.front: Why is a relative clause useful in un parc où je retrouve mes amis?
back: It adds a relevant detail about the park and connects the place to what happens there.

base_cards.front: Give the mark split for the 90-word task.
back: Communication: 10. Grammar: 5.

base_cards.front: Translate into French: I have lived here for three years, and I like my town.
back: J'habite ici depuis trois ans et j'aime ma ville.
Present + depuis describes the continuing situation.

base_cards.front: Translate into French: Last weekend, I went to Paris with my sister.
back: Le week-end dernier, je suis allé / allée à Paris avec ma sœur.
Use être and the speaker's agreement; Paris takes à.

base_cards.front: Develop J'aime le sport with a reason and a particular activity.
back: J'aime le sport parce que cela me détend. Je joue au tennis avec mes amis le samedi.
The reason explains the preference; the activity, company and time provide specific detail.

base_cards.front: Explain the difference between je travaillerai, je vais travailler and je travaillerais.
back: Je travaillerai: I will work, simple future.
Je vais travailler: I am going to work, near future.
Je travaillerais: I would work, conditional.

base_cards.front: Correct: Hier, je vais au parc. J'aime joue. Ma sœur est allé. Il y a beaucoup des magasins.
back: Hier, **je suis allé / allée** au parc.
J'aime **jouer**.
Ma sœur est **allée**.
Il y a beaucoup **de** magasins.

base_cards.front: Develop a view of your town in French with a reason, drawback and proposed improvement.
back: J'aime ma ville parce qu'elle est calme. Cependant, il n'y a pas assez de bus. Je voudrais améliorer les transports en commun pour aider les habitants.
The improvement directly addresses the stated problem. Pour + infinitive explains its purpose.

additions.front: Translate: Last Saturday, my friends and I visited a museum.
back: Samedi dernier, mes amis et moi avons visité un musée.

additions.front: Why does “mes amis et moi” take avons?
back: The group includes the speaker, so it takes the nous verb form.
Parce que nous aimons l’histoire.

additions.front: Correct: Hier, je vais au parc.
back: Hier, je suis allé(e) au parc.
Use the completed past form for this message.
Je veux travailler.
The following verb is an infinitive.
Mes amies sont gentilles.
The adjective agrees with the feminine plural subject.

additions.front: Correct: Je n’ai pas des frères.
back: Je n’ai pas de frères.
Des normally becomes de after this negative.

additions.front: Can you replace an unfamiliar museum with a cinema in a translation?
back: No. Simplify the construction if necessary, but preserve the given message rather than changing the facts.

additions.front: What should be checked for every compulsory bullet?
back: Check that it has been answered with relevant development and an appropriate time reference.

additions.front: Why is complexity not the same as length?
back: A useful relative clause, reason or contrast adds a relationship between ideas. Extra words without meaning do not develop communication.

additions.front: What should you establish before changing a verb ending?
back: Identify the subject and the intended time frame.

additions.front: What are the current Higher French writing tasks?
back: English-to-French translation, an approximately 90-word response covering three bullets, and an approximately 150-word response covering two bullets.

additions.front: Why should a memorised paragraph be adapted?
back: Its person, topic, purpose and time frame must match the actual task. Accurate but irrelevant material cannot answer a missing bullet.

additions.front: Translate: I would like to improve my town.
back: Je voudrais améliorer ma ville.
